What is OpenBot   
OpenBot is a free, open-source alternative to Grok Bot - a team of AI agents that runs locally on your own computer instead of cloud. Plug in the ChatGPT, Claude, Grok or OpenCode subscription you already have, no extra bill.   
It also has a multiplayer mode, so your whole team can share a project and talk to the same agents together, live.  
  
The problem   
Grok Bot showed where AI is headed - agents that work for you. But it runs on a Linux server in the cloud: plenty of apps just don't work there, websites often flag and block that kind of server traffic outright, it costs $200-300/month on top of what you already pay, and there's no way for a team to actually work with the same agents together.

results.title: Open-Source alternative to Grok Bot | daily.dev
results.content: OpenBot is an open-source, self-hosted platform for running AI agent "coworkers" that each get their own isolated computer (browser, files, tools). Every browser, file, or MCP action passes through a gateway that evaluates policy, records an audit entry, and only then executes, or refuses and names the rule that blocked it. Built on the AG-UI protocol, it accepts agents from any framework (LangGraph, Mastra, CrewAI, Pydantic AI, Google ADK) or hand-written endpoints. Runs via Docker Compose with PostgreSQL for storage, requires a CopilotKit Intelligence license and a model API key, and ships three example coworkers (General Assistant, Knowledge, Risk Analyst). Features include CEL-based deny-by-default policy, human handoff ("take the wheel"), encrypted credentials, and a governed MCP

If you want the smoothest, most polished version of this idea and you don't mind paying, Grok Bot is that product — once you clear the waitlist and accept the meter. For everyone else, the Grok Bot free alternative gets you most of the idea for none of the money.

| Feature | Grok Bot | OpenMausBot |
 --- 
| Price | Paid and metered, behind a waitlist | Free, runs on subscriptions you already have |
| Access | Early beta invite | GitHub download today |
| Models | Fixed, no switching | Per bot: Fable 5, Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Haiku, Codex, Grok 4.5 |
| Agent-to-agent tagging | Works | Broken in my test, for now |
| Polish | Big-company smooth | Day-one open source |

## Grok Bot Free Alternative FAQ

## The Rough Edges, Because It Launched a Day Ago

This is open source and it literally just launched, so expect some mess.

 Formatting glitches in places. It's launch-day software.
 It only runs on Claude, Codex and Grok for now.
 The approvals get repetitive.
 Agent-to-agent tagging didn't work when I tested it. Grok Bot has that working, and I'd expect a fix, but today it's broken.
 It's not a polished big-company product, and it doesn't pretend to be.
